questions.q: Which clue in a problem most strongly suggests the sliding window pattern?
o: The longest contiguous substring or subarray that satisfies a condition
Count the number of ways to climb a staircase
Find the shortest path in a weighted graph
Generate every permutation of the input
questions.w: A window over contiguous elements is updated incrementally as it slides, so one pass is enough.

questions.q: How does a hash map reduce two sum from O(n²) to O(n)?
o: It remembers values already seen, so each complement lookup takes O(1)
It sorts the array first and then compares the ends
It tries every pair but stops at the first match
It stores the array in reverse order
questions.w: For each number you look up target minus the number in the map. It costs O(n) extra memory.

questions.q: Which condition makes the two-pointers technique work on a pair-sum problem?
o: The array is sorted, so each sum shows which way to move
The array contains only positive integers and no zeros
The array length is a power of two or one less
The target value appears at least twice in the array
questions.w: If the sum is too big the right pointer moves left, and if too small the left pointer moves right, discarding values that cannot work.

questions.q: What do prefix sums let you do after one pass over the array?
o: Answer any range-sum query in O(1)
Sort the array in O(1)
Find the median without reading the data
Remove duplicates in place
questions.w: The sum of positions i to j is prefix[j+1] - prefix[i], a difference of two precomputed values.

questions.q: Which two properties usually signal a dynamic programming problem?
o: Overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure
Sorted input and unique keys
A graph with no cycles and positive weights
A fixed window size and a string input
questions.w: The same smaller problems repeat, and the best answer is built from best answers of smaller problems, so each can be computed once and reused.

questions.q: In backtracking, why do you remove the last choice after the recursive call returns?
o: To undo the choice so the next option starts from the same state
To free memory held by the recursion stack
To mark the choice as visited for ever
To sort the remaining choices
questions.w: Choose, explore, undo is the core of backtracking. Without the undo, choices would leak into later branches.

questions.q: Why does greedy coin change fail for coins 1, 3 and 4 and amount 6?
o: Taking the largest coin first gives 4+1+1 (3 coins) but 3+3 needs only 2
The amount 6 can never be made from those coins
Greedy always fails when the coins include 1
Dynamic programming also gives 3 coins
questions.w: A locally best choice is not always globally best. Dynamic programming tries all coins for each amount and finds 2.

questions.q: What should you do first when given a coding problem in an interview?
o: Clarify the requirements and constraints and work a small example
Start writing the optimised solution at once
Memorise the closest known problem and recite its answer
Ask to skip to the next question
questions.w: Clarifying inputs, size limits and edge cases avoids solving the wrong problem and often reveals the pattern.
